reader.requirement: At --std 85, every file description entry of the run unit that describes one external file connector must (a) have a LINAGE clause if any of them has one, (b) give the same integer-1 to integer-4 where specified, and (c) reference with data-name-1 to data-name-4 the same corresponding external data items; a run unit that obeys this must work with one shared page and LINAGE-COUNTER (§1985:X.4.2.4 GR1), and since the compiler enforces the rule across a compilation group, it must refuse each lettered violation there.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.DialectLevel < 2002 runs CheckFileDescriptions (the 1985 FD agreement rows, LINAGE among them); 2002 on runs CheckFormat instead
is2023 (DialectLevel >= 2023) gates the NotExternal check that a LINAGE data-name operand of an external file references an external data item (COBOL1624); at 85 it is skipped
the run-time EC-EXTERNAL-DATA-MISMATCH comparison of LinageRef runs only under an enabled ExternalChecks gate (the 2002+ exception-checking mechanism); 85 has none

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the LINAGE integers of an external connector's entries are compared (COBOL6847), at 2002 and later not; at 2023 a non-external LINAGE data item is refused (COBOL1624), at 85 not, although §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR11c already speaks of external data items

reader.notes: The 85 arm compares LINAGE operands as a string where a data-name is a wildcard and an entry without the clause is skipped, so only GR11b is enforced: GR11a's entry without a LINAGE clause and GR11c's different or non-external data items compile and run silently, while the external-item check exists but is gated to 2023. An obeying run unit works (the shared page and counter are right). If the reading that GR11 binds only the program (as the g85_bf22_05 header states) were taken, the verdict would be CONFORMS; it is PARTIAL because the compiler enforces GR11 in a compilation group and leaves out two of its three lettered items.
reader.at-2023: l11a and l11c compile clean at --std 2023 (2023 has no FD LINAGE agreement rule); l11d is refused at 2023 with COBOL1624 twice
